newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares higher, electronics lead.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares higher, electronics lead.

text.p: Singapore shares continued to rise in hectic trading on Thursday with electronic issues leading the way .
Dealers said electronic shares continue to rise to new highs on momentum and upbeat sentiment over an expected recovery in the sector in the second half.
Several technology and electronics-related stocks touched new year highs including Acer at US$2.07, Flextech at S$1.90 and Venture Manufacuring at S$5.30.
Multimedia firm Aztech, seen as a laggard in the sector, rose 3.5 cents to S$0.645 with over 10 million shares traded.
The SES electronics index leaped more than four percent to touch a new high of 150.41 before easing slightly to 150.30 at noon, up 6.05 points.
"There is some profit-taking but it has been well absorbed," said a broker with a Singapore broking firm.
Elsewhere in the market, index stocks like Cycle & Carriage and Jurong Shipyard were firmer by 30 cents and 15 cents respectively with moderate volumes.
The Straits Times Industrial Index was up by 10.69 points to 1,985.38 at noon. Volume was an active 196.97 million shares with 314 gainers thumping 69 losers.
Dealers said sentiment was also underpined by a pick-up in Malaysian issues traded over the counter. The UOB-OTC index was up 12.89 points or 1.18 percent to 1,100.73 at noon.
